articles.title: Robust inflows, pullback in shorts lift rupee to seven-month peak
articles.content: The Indian rupee saw a notable rise, achieving its peak value in seven months following a surge in foreign equity investments. Closing at 93.47 per dollar, this upswing was driven by an impressive influx of $10 billion this month. Additionally, traders observed substantial movements in the dollar-rupee non-deliverable forward market as bearish positions were unwound.

articles.title: Millions launches US stocks, ETFs investment facility for Indian investors
articles.content: Investment platform Millions, operated by Raise Financial Services, has launched US stocks and ETFs on its app. This new feature allows Indian investors to make fractional investments and use systematic investment plans. The launch is supported by the International Financial Services Centres Authority under GIFT City's framework. Millions provides mutual funds, stocks, and zero brokerage, with no account fees or maintenance charges.

articles.title: Sebi may limit leveraged stock bets to curb volatility: Report
articles.content: India's markets regulator is exploring potential limits on leveraged stock purchases amid increasing retail participation. Concerns have arisen as margin-funded stock bets have reached record levels in recent months. Discussions are ongoing regarding hard limits tied to a company's free float to manage risks effectively. While the regulator aims to mitigate market instability, it seeks to avoid disrupting retail investors' positions.

articles.title: South Korean shares close at over 9-month low on Nvidia caution
articles.content: South Korean shares experienced a significant decline of more than 2% amid concerns affecting chipmakers. The benchmark KOSPI closed at its lowest level since February due to persistent selling pressure. Foreign investors were noted as net sellers of shares worth approximately 1.4 trillion won. The Korean won weakened slightly against the dollar during this trading period. Additionally, South Korea's benchmark bond yields fell as market activities shifted.

articles.title: Australia sells A$6 billion of new 2057 Treasury bond
articles.content: The Australian government's debt management arm made a significant move by issuing A$6 billion in a new Treasury bond set to mature in June 2057, boasting a yield to maturity of 5.62%. With bids totaling A$25.25 billion, investor interest remains strong. The settlement for this issuance is earmarked for November 24, with no additional issuances expected until March 2027. Five prominent banks took lead roles in this offering.

articles.title: Indian bonds gain as oil slide eases rate hike concerns
articles.content: Indian government bonds saw an increase as oil prices dropped significantly in early trading. This decline in crude prices is expected to ease inflationary pressures and reduce concerns about aggressive rate hikes. The benchmark 6.94% 2036 bond yield fell to 7.2813% during early trading hours. Lower oil prices are particularly beneficial for India, supporting the local rupee and current account deficit.

articles.title: JGB yields climb as buyers hold back on long-dated debt
articles.content: Japanese government bond yields generally increased on Tuesday except for the benchmark 10-year yield, which fell. The 20-year and 30-year JGB yields reached their highest levels in about a month and since October. Investors are wary of taking interest-rate risks ahead of the 20-year bond auction. Concerns about falling equities may also affect bond supply-demand conditions amidst uncertainty.

Strong Indian equities, lower oil prices and improving earnings boosted sentiment, while foreign investors increasingly reversed their bearish positioning.
